text: dsh-memory-tree 是面向 DSH 的长期记忆插件，适用于桌面、Web 与命令行宿主。它在会话事件中收集对话，并在每轮开始前检索相关记忆注入上下文；记忆按项目和全局空间隔离，解析为可寻址的 AST 节点并存入分层 SQLite。用户还可通过工具搜索、保存笔记、查看统计、整理记忆和轮转存储。适合需要跨会话找回项目决策与历史讨论的用户。默认使用 Pollinations 嵌入服务；也可配置兼容 API 或本地 Ollama，并设置相应凭据。

dsh-memory-tree adds persistent memory to DSH. It captures exchanges, stores project and shared notes in tiered SQLite, and recalls context in later turns. Tools support search, saving, statistics, cleanup, and rotation. Pollinations is the default embedding provider; local Ollama is configurable.

Help my DSH agent recall relevant decisions from earlier sessions.

dsh-memory-tree 的功能「自动捕获对话」：插件监听用户与助手消息，将对话缓冲成交流并写入记忆引擎；可配置是否包含助手回复、长度限制和排除会话。
dsh-memory-tree 的功能「按需自动回忆」：每轮第一步前提取用户问题并检索相关节点，将有限长度的记忆块追加到上下文；可关闭自动注入。
dsh-memory-tree 的功能「记忆工具组」：提供 mem_recall、mem_store、mem_stats、mem_dream 和 mem_rotate，让 agent 搜索、保存、查看、整理及轮转记忆。
dsh-memory-tree 的功能「分层存储与空间隔离」：引擎按项目目录和全局空间组织记忆，并支持热、温、冷 SQLite 存储轮转；检索可指定项目或全局范围。
Captured text is sent to the configured embedding service; local Ollama is also supported.
我想按项目隔离记忆，又能主动搜索所有项目共用的笔记。
Can the agent save a note now and retrieve it by topic in a later session?

dsh-memory-tree README · dsh-memory-tree：Your agent forgets. A task ends, the context is gone, the compaction summary dies with the
session, and a new task in the same project starts from zero. Notes you saved last month never
surface when a new idea connects to them.

This plugin makes memory an **asset on disk** instead of a consumable in the context window:

dsh-memory-tree README · dsh-memory-tree：- **captures** every user/assistant exchange in the background,
- **indexes** it as an AST tree of addressable nodes with embeddings and soft similarity links,
- **recalls** relevant nodes before each turn and injects one bounded `<memory-recall>` block,
- **tiers** the data into hot/warm/cold SQLite files so the active file never grows with age,
- and exposes `mem_recall`, `mem_store`, `mem_stats`, `mem_dream`, `mem_rotate` as tools.
dsh-memory-tree README · dsh-memory-tree：No external service. No native build. One directory you can copy, inspect, back up, or delete.

dsh-memory-tree README · Compatibility：Tested with DSH **0.2.1-rc.3** (bundled Node 24) on Windows and Linux CI, Node 22 and 24; Node ≥ 22.5
for CLI use. The plugin has no native build and no runtime dependency tree of its own — it resolves
DSH's `@deepseek-ai/*` packages from the profile.

`package.json` declares `engines.dsh` (`^0.2.1-alpha.2`), and `npm run compat` in CI asserts the
session-format injection rules too, so a DSH rule change turns CI red instead of breaking an install.

dsh-memory-tree README · Compatibility：| What breaks | What happens |
|---|---|
| The host rejects the injected message (e.g. another source-kind change) | auto-recall is switched off after that turn and logged; capture and the `mem_recall` tool keep working |
| `agent/pre-step` is renamed or gone | auto-recall is off, everything else stays |
| `session/event` is gone | capture is off, the tools and recall stay |
| The engine child process crashes | it restarts; the conversation is unaffected |
dsh-memory-tree README · Compatibility：`mem_stats` prints a `compat:` line showing normal, degraded or off.

dsh-memory-tree README · Why not just a vector store?：| Need | Flat chunk RAG | This project |
|---|---|---|
| Find similar text | ✅ | ✅ embeddings |
| Address a memory ("the optogenetics idea") | ❌ anonymous chunks | ✅ unique AST paths |
| Surface a hit's section / siblings | ❌ | ✅ one-hop tree activation |
| Explain why something was recalled | ❌ one cosine number | ✅ six named score terms + audit rows |
| Bound the active database | ❌ grows forever | ✅ hot/warm/cold rotation |
| Work offline / no vendor | depends | ✅ Ollama or a deterministic fake embedder |
| Be inspected by a human | depends | ✅ Markdown mirror beside SQLite |

dsh-memory-tree README · How it works：```
session/event ──▶ capture buffer (per session, coalesced per exchange)
                    │
                    ▼
              AST parse ──▶ nodes (path, kind, title, content)

Scoring (see [PRINCIPLES](docs/PRINCIPLES.md#4-scoring) for why each term exists):

```
base = (0.55·cosine + 0.20·lexical + 0.25·rank-agreement) × tier-weight
     + one hop: parent ×0.55, similar neighbour ×0.55·similarity
     + priors: 0.06·importance + 0.05·recency(45d) + 0.03·usage
```

dsh-memory-tree README · Measured behaviour：`node scripts/bench.mjs --sizes 1000,10000,30000` on this machine (Windows, Node 24, fake
embedder so the numbers measure storage + retrieval, not the network):

| nodes | DB size | recall p50 | recall p95 | rotation | hot file after rotation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,001 | 5.4 MB | 11.6 ms | 15.2 ms | 137 docs, 0.5 s | **0.36 MB** |
| 10,003 | 54.1 MB | 55.9 ms | 68.4 ms | 1,370 docs, 6.0 s | **2.48 MB** |
| 30,002 | 162.6 MB | 191.2 ms | 258.3 ms | 4,109 docs, 25.6 s | **7.23 MB** |

dsh-memory-tree README · Storage tiers：| Tier | File | Default age | Vectors | Recall weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hot | `memory.db` | < 30 days | kept | 1.00 |
| warm | `memory-warm.db` | 30–180 days | kept | 0.90 |
| cold | `memory-cold.db` | > 180 days | kept (`dropColdVectors: true` to drop) | 0.78 |

dsh-memory-tree README · Storage tiers：Rotation runs on a timer (6 h), after startup, and on demand via `mem_rotate`. Whole documents
move with their nodes and embeddings; nothing is deleted. Dropping cold vectors keeps the archive
keyword-searchable at a fraction of the size.

Set `storage.tiered: false` for the old single-file behaviour.

dsh-memory-tree README · FAQ：**Does it slow down as memory grows?**
Recall is a scan over the active spaces: 12 ms at 1k, 56 ms at 10k, 191 ms at 30k nodes on this
machine. Tiering keeps the hot file small; past ~50k nodes, wire up `sqlite-vec` behind
`store.listVectors` (the seam exists for it).

**Can I use it without a cloud key?**
Yes. `embedding.preset: ollama` with `bge-m3` runs fully local, and `embedding.fake: true` gives a
deterministic offline embedder for demos and tests.

dsh-memory-tree README · FAQ：**What if I change embedding models?**
Vectors from different models are incomparable. Use a new `dataDir` (or delete the tier files) and
let it re-index; the Markdown mirror keeps the raw text.

**Two machines?**
Copy `$DSH_HOME/memory-tree/` once, then never let both write the same SQLite file. One-way sync or
git on the Markdown mirror only. Multi-writer CRDT sync is on the roadmap.

dsh-memory-tree README · FAQ：**Does it replace `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`?**
No — those are instructions you maintain; this is history the agent accumulates. They complement
each other.

**Is my conversation sent anywhere?**
Only the text chunks you capture, to your configured embedding endpoint. No telemetry, no upload
of the database.
